newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Jerusalem Committee to meet in Morocco on March 27.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem Committee to meet in Morocco on March 27.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Saturday the Jerusalem Committee of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) would hold a meeting on March 27 in Morocco to discuss Israeli settlement plans in the holy city.
Mubarak, who was speaking at the end of a 24-hour visit to Rabat, said the ministerial meeting was agreed upon during talks on Friday night with King Hassan, chairman of the committee.

"After talks with his Majesty King Hassan, it was decided to convene al-Qods (Jerusalem) Committee on March 27-28, 1997, to examine the latest developments related to the holy city," Mubarak told reporters at Rabat airport before flying to Cairo.
The 70-minute talks between the Egyptian and Moroccan heads of state "were also focused on the Middle East peace process and bilateral relations", Mubarak added but gave no other details.
The 15-member committee was set up by an OIC summit back in 1975 with the aim of preventing the city, holy to Moslems, Christians and Jews, being "Judaised" by Israel.
Israel said this week it was going ahead with plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews between Arab East Jerusalem and Bethlemen, a move that has fuelled Palestinian anger.

Asked about a possibility of convening an Arab summit to discuss the crisis facing the peace process, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told Reuters: "The idea of holding an Arab summit exists...But the priorty for Arab and Moslem countries is al-Qods issue."
He said that Mubarak's visit to the United States was "important and positive".
"We want that Washington, which is the main sponsor of the peace process, to continue to play the role of an independent and honest mediator," Moussa said.

Mubarak, who arrived in Morocco from United States on Thursday, was the third Arab leader -- after King Hussein of Jordan and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat -- to visit Morocco in the last four weeks.
Arafat said after a visit to Morocco late last month that he and King Hassan had also agreed on the need to hold an urgent meeting of the Al Qods committee.
The committee is made up of Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Guinea, Indonesia, Iran, Niger, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Senegal, Iraq, Syria, Mauritania and the Palestinian Authority.
